Pilot · about 25 minutes

Is this product an AI? Is it an agent?

A prediction market lets people bet on whether something will happen — an election result, a match, a price. Polymarket is the largest one. Every question is a market, and every market has a price between 0 and 1: that price is the crowd's probability that the event happens.

Many independent tools are built on top of Polymarket — dashboards, wallets, trading bots, copy-trading services, AI forecasters. Each card shows one such product through its own website, captured for this study, so you never leave this page.

For each product you answer two yes/no questions, defined below. The definitions stay beside you on every card. This is a test of the instructions, not of you — if anything is unclear, say so in the box at the end.

1. AI Does a large language model predict the market's probability?

The product uses a large language model — GPT, ChatGPT, Claude, OpenClaw, or a comparable AI language model — to predict the probability of a market outcome.

Every Polymarket market has a price, and that price is the market's implied probability. A product is AI when a language model forms its own estimate of that probability — the gap between its estimate and the market price is the predicted opportunity it offers the trader.

YES
The site says an LLM forecasts, estimates, scores, or reasons about how likely an outcome is — AI-generated odds, probabilities, forecasts, edge, or mispricing against the market price.
NO
No language model produces a probability or forecast. Analytics, dashboards, wallets, terminals, exchanges, alerts, news feeds and copy trading are not AI on their own.

Do not code AI merely because of generic automation, rankings, “smart” scores, or “AI” in the product's name or branding. The site must tie a language model to predicting how likely an outcome is.

2. Agent Does the product execute trades automatically?

The product places trades by itself, without the user entering each order — automated trading strategies, bots, rule-based execution, and copy trading.

The test is who presses the button. If the product executes on the trader's behalf once it is set up, it is an agent. If a person must place every order themselves, it is not.

YES
The site says the product automatically places, executes, mirrors, or copies trades, runs trading strategies, or trades while the user is away.
NO
It is analytics, alerts, a wallet, an exchange, research, news, portfolio tracking, or a manual trading terminal only.

Do not code Agent merely because there is a trading interface, because users can execute trades by hand, or because it sends signals and alerts a person must act on.

1

Read the site in the card. The screenshot scrolls, and the Page text tab holds the whole page — check it before answering.

2

Answer Yes only when the site says so. A name like “PolyAI” proves nothing on its own.

3

The two questions are independent. A product can be one, both, or neither.

4

If the site is blank or dead, tick No usable site and move on.

5

Work alone. Do not discuss the products with other people while coding.

The definitions stay beside you on every card, so you do not need to memorise them.
